verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 48.49
verses.english: Linked Discourses 48.49

verses.pali: 5. Jarāvagga
verses.english: 5. Old Age

verses.pali: Piṇḍolabhāradvājasutta
verses.english: About Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer

verses.pali: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
verses.english: So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmatā piṇḍolabhāradvājena aññā byākatā hoti:
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer had declared enlightenment:

verses.pali: “khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī”ti.
verses.english: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. Then they said,

verses.pali: “Āyasmatā, bhante, piṇḍolabhāradvājena aññā byākatā:
‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti.
Kiṁ nu kho, bhante, atthavasaṁ sampassamānena āyasmatā piṇḍolabhāradvājena aññā byākatā:
verses.english: “What reason does Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer see for doing this?”

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti?
“Tiṇṇannaṁ kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā piṇḍolabhāradvājena bhikkhunā aññā byākatā:
verses.english: “It’s because Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer has developed and cultivated three faculties that he declares enlightenment:

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti.
verses.english: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’

verses.pali: Katamesaṁ tiṇṇannaṁ?
verses.english: What three?

verses.pali: Satindriyassa, samādhindriyassa, paññindriyassa—
verses.english: The faculties of mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

verses.pali: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṁ indriyānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā piṇḍolabhāradvājena bhikkhunā aññā byākatā:
verses.english: It’s because Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer has developed and cultivated these three faculties that he declares enlightenment.

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti.
Imāni ca, bhikkhave, tīṇindriyāni kimantāni?
verses.english: What’s the culmination of these three faculties?

verses.pali: Khayantāni.
verses.english: They culminate in ending.

verses.pali: Kissa khayantāni?
verses.english: In the ending of what?

verses.pali: Jātijarāmaraṇassa.
verses.english: Of rebirth, old age, and death.

verses.pali: ‘Jātijarāmaraṇaṁ khayan’ti kho, bhikkhave, sampassamānena piṇḍolabhāradvājena bhikkhunā aññā byākatā:
verses.english: It’s because he sees that they culminate in the ending of rebirth, old age, and death that Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer declares enlightenment:

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti.
verses.english: ‘I understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”’”

verses.pali: Navamaṁ.
